lines.text: If a girl in a white dress asks you for a ride on Archer Avenue... don't stop. Just don't.
Chicago, winter, two in the morning. I was driving home from a dance on Archer Avenue.
Then I saw her. On the side of the road, in the snow. A girl in a white dress. No coat.
Can you take me home? It's not far.
She got in. Her hand touched mine. It was cold. Ice cold.
She didn't talk. She just stared out the window. And she smelled like flowers. Old flowers.
Stop here. This is where I live.
We were in front of the gates of Resurrection Cemetery.
I turned to ask what she meant... and the seat was empty. The door was still closed.
Through the bars of the gate, I saw a white dress, walking between the graves.
They say her name is Mary. She died on her way home from a dance, almost a hundred years ago. And she's still trying to get home.
So if a girl in white waves at you on Archer Avenue... keep driving.
